newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to ease securities industry restrictions.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to ease securities industry restrictions.

text.p: South Korea will ease restrictions on the local securities industry, allowing brokerage firms to issue corporate bonds, government officials said on Tuesday.
The government also will allow local securities companies to hold up to 15 percent of shares in a single listed firm, up from the current limit of five percent, they said.
Foreign currency-denominated bonds issued by local companies will be allowed to be traded locally in the near future, they added.
A finance ministry official, who asked not to be identified, said the government steps aimed to help improve the local securities industry's competitiveness.
"The measures will be implemented as soon as possible, some from next month," he said.
Although the government will soon allow brokerage firms to issue corporate bonds, ceilings and qualifications have yet to be worked out, government officials said.

The finance ministry and the committee have agreed to let another presidential advisory committee review steps to ease requirements for establishing securities and investment trust companies, set up another stock exchange in South Korea two years later and encourage public bond sales, they said.
The Korea Stock Exchange now monopolises share trading in South Korea.

The finance ministry official said the government had agreed to accept immediately 10 of 23 recommendations made by a committee commissioned by President Kim Young-sam to draft streamlined formalities.

The 10, which also included easing qualifications for investment consultants, would be implemented as soon as necessary legal steps are taken, he said but declined to say what the other six measures are.
He said the ministry did not immediately agree to committee recommendations to allow institutional investors to utilise margin loans and remove restrictions on setting up securities firms.
